claims.text: A request travels forward through Kestrel, routing, and each registered middleware in order, reaching the endpoint only if nothing short-circuits first.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Middleware fundamentals and Routing fundamentals

claims.text: Once a response is produced (by the endpoint or by a short-circuit), it travels back out through every middleware that ran on the way in, in the reverse of the order they ran in.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Middleware fundamentals (middleware order / write custom middleware)

claims.text: A middleware registered before the one that short-circuits still runs its own after-next code on the way back out, because from its own view next simply returned.
OrdersController.Get(int id), which has no [Authorize] attribute, returns 404 via NotFound() when no order with the given id is found.

Sending GET /api/v1/orders/999999 (a nonexistent order) to the running stage-1 lab returns 404, and docker compose logs api shows a RequestLoggingMiddleware line for that request reporting status 404.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang stage-1 lab: docker compose logs api after curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders/999999

claims.text: In DonHang.Api/Program.cs, the forward order of wiring calls is ExceptionHandlingMiddleware, RequestLoggingMiddleware, UseCors, UseAuthentication, UseAuthorization, MapControllers; the reverse order for a response is the same list backward.

self_check.notes: Applied the corrected mental model from the previous lesson's review (routing matches the endpoint automatically, before user middleware runs) throughout, to avoid repeating that error. Try it uses a new example (GET a nonexistent order, 404 via normal endpoint logic) rather than repeating the previous lesson's short-circuit example, to test the 'response decided late' point specifically.
